function: Transmit power control of LEO satellites for over-the-air (AirComp) gradient aggregation in federated learning, minimizing total energy under a convergence constraint (p. 1, p. 3).
system: N=15 LEO satellites to one ground station, scalar channel per satellite (single antennas implied); no RIS; 200 MHz bandwidth, carrier band not stated (p. 2, p. 4).
method: Federated learning (ResNet9, mini-batch gradient descent) with OTA gradient aggregation; power set each round by OPCO, a heuristic local search, not learned (p. 2, p. 4).
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. CSCG (Rayleigh) channels, unit variance, with CSI error variance 1e-3; CIFAR-10 partitioned non-iid (Dirichlet alpha 0.1) (p. 2, p. 4, p. 5).
test_conditions: One setting throughout: N=15 satellites, pmin 20 W, pmax 50 W, R 10 Mbps, 200 MHz, CSI error 1e-3; accuracy on CIFAR-10 test data (p. 4, p. 5).
baselines: MTP and MTT (OFDMA, fixed pmin or pmax), OTA-MTP and OTA-MTT (OTA, fixed pmin or pmax), and GAPC gradient-aware power control from [8] (p. 4, p. 5).
metrics: Test accuracy versus total energy consumption; total and per-round energy, number of rounds, and total transmission time to reach 70% accuracy (p. 5).
complexity: Time complexity of Algorithm 1 (OPCO) is O(N), linear in the number of satellites; no runtime or operation counts (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "follows i.i.d. circularly symmetric complex Gaussian (CSCG) distribution with zero mean and unit variance" (custom i.i.d. Gaussian channel; no 3GPP TR 38.811 or other standard model, ray tracing, or measured data).
q2_support: p. 4: "We set pmin = 20 W, pmax = 50 W, and R = 10 Mbps in all experiments" (single configuration with N = 15 satellites; the FL model is only tested on held-out CIFAR-10 data, no new scenario, constellation size, or channel).
q3_support: p. 5: "optimizes satellite transmission power in OTA FL by adaptively adjusting it for each client during each round as in [8]" (GAPC, earlier published aggregation design); p. 5: "All satellites transmit simultaneously over the shared bandwidth at pmin with OTA aggregation" (OTA-MTP, fixed power, non-learned); p. 5: "OPCO consistently requires less energy consumption compared to all benchmarks".
q4_support: p. 4: "The time complexity of Algorithm 1 is O (N ), scaling linearly with the number of satellites" (order of complexity of the proposed power control, i.e., the aggregation design).
q5_support: p. 4: "We adopt the CIFAR10 dataset and conduct the experiments using a ResNet9 architecture" (learning-task dataset only; channels are simulated, p. 2; no code or data link).
notes: Included as area 7: the paper designs transmit power control for over-the-air (AirComp) aggregation of FL gradients from LEO satellites to a ground station (p. 1, p. 2). OTA FL passes the no_learning check by rule, although OPCO itself is a heuristic local search, not learned (p. 4). Area 6 (power control of satellite links) also fits; 7 wins by precedence. Check 6: the link is single-antenna without RIS (scalar CSCG coefficient per satellite, one GS, p. 2; Fig. 1, p. 3); I applied 'OTFS and NTN works admit single-antenna links' to this LEO-satellite work. If the reviewer limits that exception to works of areas 4 and 6, the decision becomes exclude, system, p. 2. q3: GAPC reproduces the published power control of [8] (Zhang and Tao, IEEE TWC 2021), taken as the earlier aggregation design; fixed-power OTA-MTP/OTA-MTT and OFDMA MTP/MTT are the non-learned baselines; all are compared on total energy to reach accuracy (Fig. 2, p. 5). q1: the elevation-angle dependence of the channel gain is only discussed (p. 4, citing [10]), not simulated. q4 quote keeps the extracted spacing of O(N).
